terms.register: Plaut., Ter.; Verg. and the poets
evidence: Plaut. Aul. 721: heu mē miserum, miserē periī
terms.comment: The plain cry of grief or pain, often with the accusative of exclamation (heu mē miserum) or doubled.

evidence: Hor. C. 2.14.1: ēheu fugācēs, Postume, Postume
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: pain or grief, often with quam. It notes that many editors print heu heu for it in the poets.

evidence: Verg. A. 2.274: ei mihi, quālis erat
terms.comment: Lewis & Short (s.v. hei): grief or fear, “freq. joined with mihi”.

terms.grammar: with the dative (vae mihi, vae victīs), rarely the accusative
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: “like the Gr. οὐαί and our woe!”. For the milder vae miserō mihi see oh dear!.

phrases.latin: ēheu fugācēs, Postume, Postume, lābuntur annī
phrases.english: alas, Postumus, Postumus, the fleeting years slip by

phrases.latin: ei mihi, quālis erat, quantum mūtātus ab illō
phrases.english: ah me, how he looked! how changed from the man he was
alas, poor me, I’m wretchedly undone

phrases.latin: ēheu, quom ego plūs minusve fēcī quam mē aequom fuit.
phrases.english: alas, that I did more or less than I should have!

sources: Lewis & Short: heu · Lewis & Short: eheu · Lewis & Short: hei · Lewis & Short: vae
